Addis Ababa Declaration on ECO Care in Africa
Download PDF

Adopted at the inaugural All-African ECO Care Congress, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, March 2026

Addis Ababa Declaration on ECO Care in Africa

Emergency, Critical and Operative Care — a continental commitment to universal health coverage, quality, and patient safety.

Congress All-African ECO Care Congress 2026
Dates 27–29 March 2026
Venue Stay Easy International Hotel

Preamble

Who we are and why we gathered

We, participants of the inaugural All-African Emergency, Critical and Operative (ECO) Care Congress, convened in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from 27-29 March 2026.

We include representatives of Ministries of Health, academic and healthcare institutions, professional societies, research networks, and international partners.

Recognising the growing burden of critical illness, surgical conditions, and emergency care needs across Africa, and the persistent inequities in access, quality, and patient safety.

Reaffirming our commitment, as Member States and partners aligned with the World Health Organisation, to strengthen integrated emergency, critical, and operative care systems in line with World Health Assembly Resolution WHA 78.2.

Drawing on evidence from continental and global initiatives, including African surgical and critical illness outcome studies, demonstrating preventable mortality.

Acknowledging progress in expanding services and strengthening systems, while recognising that fragmentation, limited use of patient-level data, and variability in care quality continue to affect outcomes.

Core Principles

What we affirm

I

Access to timely, safe, and high-quality ECO care is fundamental to universal health coverage.

II

Quality and patient safety must be central to all health system strengthening efforts.

III

Data must be used to drive continuous learning, improvement, and accountability.

IV

Collaboration across disciplines, sectors, and countries is essential for sustainable impact.

Priority Actions

What we commit to

1
Strengthening integrated ECO care systems

Advance coordinated delivery of emergency, critical, and operative care across all levels of the health system, ensuring continuity from first contact to definitive care.

2
Advancing quality and patient safety

Embed quality improvement and patient safety into routine care, including the use of standards, audits, and feedback systems to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality.

3
Scaling Essential Emergency and Critical Care (EECC)

Advance implementation of EECC as a minimum standard for life-saving clinical care, alongside strengthening essential resources for ECO care (EREC), including infrastructure, workforce, and system capacity, aligned with WHO guidance.

4
Leveraging data for action and accountability

Strengthen and integrate routine reporting systems with patient-level data platforms to enable real-time decision-making, continuous improvement, and system accountability.

5
Investing in workforce capacity and leadership

Strengthen the capacity, support, and leadership of the health workforce across the ECO care continuum.

6
Promoting context-relevant innovation

Support the development and scale-up of locally appropriate, cost-effective innovations that improve access, efficiency, and quality of care.

7
Strengthening partnerships and regional collaboration

Enhance collaboration among governments, Africa CDC, WHO, academic institutions, and partners to align priorities and accelerate implementation.

8
Advancing research and implementation science

Promote and, where possible, finance collaborative, multicountry research and implementation efforts to generate context-specific evidence and inform policy and practice.

2026–2028

Initial measurable directions

Non-binding but action-oriented, we will work collectively toward:

Expanding national adoption and scale-up of EECC

Strengthening patient-level data systems and quality improvement platforms

Improving the use of data for decision-making at the facility and national levels

Advancing multicountry collaborative research initiatives

Continental Platform

Building an All-African ECO Care Institute

We recognise this congress as the starting point of a sustained continental platform for ECO care collaboration. We commit to advancing the development of an All-African ECO Care platform, with the aim of evolving into an All-African ECO Care Institute to support research, training, innovation, and system strengthening across the continent.

This process will be collaborative, inclusive, and aligned with existing regional and global frameworks.

Call to action

We call upon governments, the World Health Organisation, Africa CDC, academic and research institutions, and development partners to align efforts, strengthen coordination, and invest in scalable, evidence-based solutions that advance innovation, quality, and patient safety in ECO care.

Conclusion

Adopted in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, March 2026

This declaration reflects the shared commitment of participants and partners engaged in the inaugural All-African ECO Care Congress and will serve as a foundation for ongoing collaboration, implementation, and accountability across the continent.
